sentences.text: In AC circuits with inductors and capacitors, voltage and current are out of phase.
Real Power P, measured in Watts, is the actual power converted into useful work and heat: P = V_rms × I_rms × cos(theta).
Reactive Power Q, measured in VAR, is the power bouncing between the source and reactive fields: Q = V_rms × I_rms × sin(theta).
Apparent Power S, measured in Volt-Amps (VA), is the vector combination: S = sqrt(P² + Q²).
The Power Factor is cos(theta) = P / S.
